newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nando's soars in busy JSE debut.
newsitem.headline: Nando's soars in busy JSE debut.

text.p: Nando's Group Holdings made a firm debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Friday, with nearly two million shares traded in the first 30 minutes of trade.
The company listed 192.74 shares of 100 cents each on the Beverages, Hotel and Leisure sector of the JSE.
"It is a good opening. A number of investors who have a lot of the stock are trying to get rid of it at these prices," a dealer said

The shares opened at 150 cents, jumping 50 percent on its issue price of 100 cents, before settling at 138 cents. By 0800 GMT some 1.61 million shares valued at over 2.37 million rand had changed hands. The share was the most actively trade on the bourse.
Nandos chief financial officer Bobby Favish said the listing was proceeding well.
"We are very happy with the listing. We see it as a first step in the long journey to become a major plyer in the world," Favish told Reuters.
Dealers were mixed on whether there was still upward potential in the share price with some saying it could close at around 128 cents and some saying it would end well above that.
Its initial public offer to raise 15 million rand was 24 times over-subscribed and had brought in 361 million rand.

Nando's, which has shown heady growth in number of outlets and profits in the past 10 years and more recently moved aggressively offshore, has forecast earnings growth at 6.25 cents a share in the year to end-February 1998, compared with an historical figure of 5.15 the year before.
